Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Pokeweed

The catalogue remembers pokeweed in food, medicinal, and dye traditions. It stresses that knowledge of the plant mattered because of its toxicity. The berry’s color also appears in the account as a material for marking and dyeing.1

The catalogue repeatedly warns that pokeweed can be poisonous and describes careful preparation as essential.1

Places named in the catalogue

Shinnecock territories.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF p. 14. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
